dashboard.guidaP4: At the bottom of the dashboard you'll find each goalkeeper's scorecard with a radar of their characteristics: a quick season summary without opening the full statistics.
dashboard.introSetup: It only takes a few minutes to get your season ready. Start with the first step: the others unlock on their own as you go.
dashboard.aiutoBox: In the <comeIniziare>Getting started</comeIniziare> section you’ll find the full guide, or write to us from <contatti>Contacts</contatti>.
dashboard.guidaP1: The dashboard is your starting point: it immediately shows the past trainings and matches still to be rated (in red), the scheduled next training and the matches in the next 7 days.
dashboard.guidaP2: The yellow “Goalkeepers to watch” box automatically flags goalkeepers with at least 2 absences in the last 3 call-ups, a significant drop in performance (−1.5 average points) or a goal past its deadline not yet achieved.
dashboard.guidaP3: Here you also find the measurement reminders for goals coming due, so you know when it’s time to record a new test.

partite.guidaP1: Add games with “+ New match”: date, category, opponent, home/away and result. Open each match to enter the goalkeeper evaluations: attendance, rating, points and notes. Clean sheets are calculated automatically from matches where the goalkeeper was present and conceded zero goals.
partite.guidaP2: The match type matters in statistics: friendlies do not affect league averages and are counted separately. Use the “League” type for official games.
partite.guidaP3: To delete multiple matches in bulk (e.g. added by mistake) use the Recurrences → Bulk deletion section, where you can filter by category, date range and presence or absence of evaluations.
partite.guidaP4: You can also set the meeting time and the kick-off time of the game: they appear in the match sheet and in the calendar preview.

portieri.guidaP5: Goalkeepers can rate each session with 1 to 5 stars, plus feedback and a note. They can only do so if they are marked present and the session has already taken place: future sessions and absences stay read-only. From their own login they also see the mark and notes you entered.
portieri.guidaP1: Add goalkeepers with “+ New” and enroll them in a category of the active season. From the goalkeeper’s profile you can edit all personal data, the photo, the shirt number and the enrollment category. To send access to the goalkeeper use the Invitations section: create an invite link and the goalkeeper registers on their own, getting automatically linked to their profile.
portieri.guidaP2: The goalkeeper page also has Objectives (set targets with a deadline and track their status), Statistics (attendance, averages, growth index), Trend (month-by-month data, monthly or cumulative) and Journey (season growth timeline). Tags are managed directly on the profile.
portieri.guidaP3: To deactivate a goalkeeper without deleting them (e.g. they are no longer in the team but you want to keep the historical data) use the Active/Inactive toggle on their profile.
portieri.guidaP4: The profile also includes Announced absences: flag in advance the days the goalkeeper will be absent and they appear in the calendar, without affecting attendance or statistics. In the Goals tab you can link tests with a target value and record measurements over time: progress is then calculated automatically from the tests. Injuries marked in the evaluation grid appear on the profile and are excluded from statistics (shown with 🩹).

calendario.daValutarePortiere: Trainings to rate: {n}. Open them from the calendar and leave your rating.
calendario.guidaP1: Click on the day number to create a new training on that date. You can also select any day (even empty): the + New training and + New match buttons at the top will use that date. Trainings in green are already rated, in red they still need rating. Matches appear in purple: dark if already played, light if upcoming. Click any block to open it.
calendario.guidaP2: Inside a training you can: mark attendance, enter a rating and per-parameter scores for each goalkeeper, add the session’s drills, and enable the “No evaluation” flag if the training took place but you don’t want to enter ratings (in that case it still appears as green/rated in the calendar). You can also merge two categories into a single shared training directly from the form.
calendario.guidaP3: To delete multiple trainings or matches in bulk use the Recurrences → Bulk deletion section, where you can filter by category, date range and presence or absence of evaluations.
calendario.guidaP4: When you click a day, the preview also shows the announced absences (goalkeepers with a scheduled absence on that date) and, for matches, the meeting and kick-off times. In a training’s evaluation grid you can also mark injuries, which are then excluded from statistics.

statistiche.guidaP5: Besides the table you'll find the Growth Index (0-100, combining objectives achieved, training and match trends and attendance), the skills radar, the category ranking sortable by any KPI, the session rating charts and the team trend. In the Feedback tab you choose how many comments to show per page (10, 20, 50 or all), newest first.
statistiche.guidaP1: The statistics show for each goalkeeper: attendance out of the category’s total trainings, average rating of trainings and league matches (friendlies are excluded from the averages), clean sheets (matches played without conceding) and total points accumulated in matches.
statistiche.guidaP2: The Feedback tab collects all the comments written by goalkeepers in their self-evaluations, with the rating each goalkeeper gave to their own session. It is useful to compare the goalkeeper’s perception with the rating you assigned as staff.
statistiche.guidaP3: The statistics always refer to the active season. To view previous seasons use the Archive section.
statistiche.guidaP4: Sessions where a goalkeeper is injured are excluded from the averages (shown with 🩹). In the Goalkeeper comparison, besides attendance, you can pick a metric from the menu and compare the average of the individual evaluation items (technique, RPE, etc.) between goalkeepers or by category.

comeIniziare.introPortiere: Here are the main sections of GKSeason and how to use them as a goalkeeper.
comeIniziare.introAllenatore: Follow these steps in order to set up GKSeason and start using it with your team.
comeIniziare.faqBox: The FAQ now have their own dedicated page, more complete and organized by topic: <faqLink>go to Frequently asked questions →</faqLink>

passiAllenatore.d: Check that there is an active season. Set the name, start and end dates, club name and logo.
Activate and order the categories (teams) for the current season. Without active categories you cannot enroll goalkeepers.
Customize the dropdown values (drill types, preferred foot, origin…).
Choose which parameters to use in training evaluations (technique, coming off the line, footwork…).
Add goalkeepers with complete personal data and enroll them in a category. You can set goals, tags and view the growth path from each goalkeeper profile.
Create an invite link for each goalkeeper and send it: they register and get automatically linked to their profile.
For each category set the fixed training days and times, then click "Generate season trainings" to create all the dates in bulk. From here you can also delete trainings or matches in bulk.
Build your drill library with title, type and image. You can add them to each training from the Drills tab in the session.
Open a training to mark attendance, enter per-parameter evaluations, add drills and enable the "No evaluation" flag if the session took place without giving ratings.
Enter games with result and evaluations (attendance, rating, points per goalkeeper). Friendlies do not affect league averages.
View attendance, average ratings, clean sheets and points for each goalkeeper. The Feedback tab collects the self-evaluations written by goalkeepers.
Consult past seasons in read-only mode and export the data to CSV or PDF.
Complete your details (photo, contacts, availability) to appear in the public coach search.

passiPortiere.d: Complete your details: photo, contacts, height, preferred foot. Name, surname and category are managed by the staff.
See the trainings you are enrolled in. Where you are marked present you can leave your self-evaluation: personal rating, comment on the session and a private note visible only to you.
Consult your category’s matches: date, opponent, result and your evaluation entered by the staff.
See your season progress: attendance, average training and match ratings, clean sheets and total points. The Feedback tab shows the comments you wrote.
Consult the goals the staff set for you, with deadline and progress status.
Send proposals or reports to the staff, even anonymously. You will see the status of the reply here.

suggerimenti.intro: Have an idea to improve GKSeason or found a problem? Write it here — we read them all.
suggerimenti.emailPlaceholder: to get back to you if needed
suggerimenti.guidaP1: For goalkeepers: send proposals, reports or feedback to the staff via the form at the bottom. You can choose the category (idea, bug, improvement…) and write freely. You will see the staff’s reply here: accepted, not accepted or under review. Suggestions can also be sent anonymously.
suggerimenti.guidaP2: For staff: this page shows all the suggestions received, with sender (if logged in) or name/email (if anonymous). You can change the status of each suggestion to let the goalkeeper know how it was considered.

categorie.guidaP1: The categories you create here (e.g. First Team, Youth, U15...) are yours only: no other coach can see or edit them. You can rename them anytime from each row’s text field, or delete them with the dedicated button.

stagioni.guidaP1: You can keep several seasons active in parallel — for example one per club you work with — each with its own categories, calendar, goalkeepers and statistics completely separate. You don’t need to close one to work on another.
stagioni.guidaP2: The season you’re currently working on (your “current” one) is also shown at the top left of the menu: use that quick selector to switch between active seasons anytime, without having to deactivate one another.
stagioni.guidaP3: To create a new season (new year or new club) click “+ New season” at the top right.

parametri.guidaP1: Evaluation parameters are the criteria you use to rate each goalkeeper in trainings (e.g. technique, coming off the line, footwork, positioning). Here you can enable or disable the parameters you want to use: the active ones appear in every training’s evaluation grid.
parametri.guidaP2: The available global parameters are managed by the <sup>Supervisor</sup>. Your selection here is personal and does not affect other coaches. You can change it anytime: data already entered stays unchanged.

ricorrenze.guidaP1: First of all: recurrences only work on the categories that are active in the current season. If this page looks empty, go to My categories and make sure you’ve ticked “Active in season” for at least one category.
ricorrenze.guidaP2: Trainings: set the fixed weekly day and time of training for each category, then automatically generate all the dates in the calendar. Existing dates are not duplicated: you can regenerate safely after changes.
ricorrenze.guidaP3: Matches: two ways to fill the match calendar. Method 1 generates empty matches (date and category only) on a fixed day of the week, useful when you only know the match day and want to speed up entry — you add opponent and home/away later by opening the match. Method 2 imports a complete official schedule from an Excel file: download the template from the section, fill it with dates, opponents and home/away for the first leg, then upload it selecting the category — the app automatically creates both the first-leg and the return matches (swapping home/away).
ricorrenze.guidaP4: In the 🗑 Bulk deletion section at the bottom of the page you can delete trainings or matches in bulk within a date range. You can filter by category and choose to delete only those without evaluations (typically added by mistake), only those with evaluations, or all of them. The operation is irreversible: a confirmation is always required before proceeding.
ricorrenze.guidaP5: The Method 2 template also includes separate times for the first leg and the return (meeting and kick-off). If you re-upload the file after a correction, matches already present on those dates are updated, not duplicated.
ricorrenze.avviso: You don’t have any active category for the {nome} season yet, so there’s nothing to generate here. Go to My categories and activate at least one.

esercizi.guidaTitolo: How to use the drill library
esercizi.guidaP1: Here you’ll find your private drills. Create a drill with a title, description, type and image: you can then add it to any training directly from inside the session (Drills tab in the training).
esercizi.guidaP2: If you tick “Public” on a drill, you make it visible to other GKSeason coaches in the shared library. In the “Favourite public” section you’ll find drills from other coaches that you saved with ★ from the public library: you can use them in your trainings without recreating them.
esercizi.guidaP3: The types of drills (e.g. technical, tactical, athletic…) are managed from Supervisor → Lists. Archived drills don’t appear in the main list but stay linked to the trainings where they were added.
esercizi.guidaP4: Besides title, description and image, you can draw a tactical scheme with the built-in whiteboard: the drawing is saved with the drill and you can reopen and edit it anytime.

template.guidaP1: Create a template with a name (e.g. “Basic technical session”) and a series of drills from your library, in the order you prefer. When you create a new training in the calendar, you can choose “Duplicate from a template” instead of re-entering them every time: the drills are copied in the order set here.
template.guidaP2: Templates are yours only: if you’re a manager with linked coaches, you can also view (read-only) their templates from the supervision section.

mieiPreparatori.confermaRevoca: Revoke the connection with this coach?
mieiPreparatori.intro: Here you find all the coaches connected to your account. You can access their area to follow their work. To add a new coach, go to Invitations and create an invitation of type Coach (supervision).

archivio.guidaP1: The archive shows the complete statistics of any past season in read-only mode. Select the season from the top menu: you’ll see attendance, average ratings, clean sheets, points and the full list of matches.
archivio.guidaP2: With the Export button you can download the selected season’s data as CSV or PDF, handy for handing it to your goalkeepers or the club at the end of the year.
archivio.avvisoArchiviata: You’re viewing an archived season: the data is read-only.

supervisore.faqIntro: Questions are organized in two tabs (Coaches/staff and Goalkeepers), and within each into categories — use “+ New category” to create one, or select an existing category to view and edit only its questions. supervisore.recLegenda: The Rec 3/7/30d columns show how many records each user created in the last 3, 7 and 30 days — useful to see who is actually using the platform.

legalPrivacy.metaDescription: Information on the processing of personal data under the GDPR.
legalPrivacy.title: Privacy Policy
legalPrivacy.s1intro: The controller of personal data is:
legalPrivacy.s2intro: GKSeason collects the following categories of personal data:

s2items.desc: first name, last name, email address, password (in encrypted form).
role (coach, staff, goalkeeper), photo, city, postcode, province, approximate geographic coordinates, professional bio, experience and certificates.
trainings, matches, goalkeeper evaluations, goals, statistics, drills.
IP address, browser type, pages visited, session duration (via PostHog Analytics).
messages sent through the coach contact form or the Suggestions section (name, email, phone, message).

legalPrivacy.s3h: 3. Purposes and legal bases of processing
s3rows: Service communications (notifications, invitations, replies to suggestions)
Statistical analysis of usage to improve the service
legalPrivacy.s4intro: Data is kept only for the time strictly necessary for the purposes for which it was collected:
s4items: Account data: for the entire duration of the contractual relationship and for 10 years after termination (tax obligations).
Contact messages and suggestions: 2 years from the last exchange.
Newsletter subscription: until consent is withdrawn (unsubscribe).
legalPrivacy.s5intro: Personal data may be shared with third-party providers acting as data processors:

faqPubblica.metaDescription: Frequently asked questions about GKSeason, the platform for goalkeeper coaches and goalkeepers: features, pricing, free trial, privacy and more.
faqPubblica.title: Frequently asked questions
faqPubblica.intro: Answers to the most common questions about GKSeason.
faqPubblica.a1: GKSeason is the platform for goalkeeper coaches: manage trainings, evaluations, statistics, matches, drills and goals for your goalkeepers in a single app. Goalkeepers can follow their own progress and statistics.
faqPubblica.a2: For goalkeeper coaches at every level — from youth academies to first teams — and for goalkeepers who want to track their progress.
faqPubblica.q3: How much does it cost? Is there a free plan?
faqPubblica.a3: You can start for free with the basic features. Advanced features (full statistics, goals, automatic recurrences and more) are part of a paid subscription. Every new user also gets a free trial of all features.
faqPubblica.q4: What can I manage with GKSeason?
faqPubblica.a4: Training calendar and sessions, goalkeeper evaluations by technical parameters, statistics and growth charts, matches and performances, a drill library (with a tactical board) and individual goals.
faqPubblica.q5: How do I find a goalkeeper coach near me?
faqPubblica.a5: From the «Find coaches» section you can search by city and distance for coaches available in your area and view their profile.
faqPubblica.a6: Yes: the coach invites their goalkeepers, who get a personal area with their own profile, statistics and growth path.
faqPubblica.a7: Yes. We process data in compliance with the GDPR, with encrypted connections and restricted access. See the Privacy Policy for full details.
faqPubblica.q8: Which languages is GKSeason available in?
faqPubblica.a8: GKSeason is available in Italian, English, German and Spanish. You can switch language from the selector at any time.
